verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Lean writes the set directly in the slow coordinates (R,Z,T) that the paper obtains as the image under C_ℓ, rather than as `{C_ℓ(r,z,t) : …}`, and names the band ratio q/Q as its own existential variable q ∈ [1/2,2]. Clause by clause, with R = r/√Q, Z = z/Q^D, T = τ/Q and q̂ = q/Q: `0 ≤ p.2.2` is τ ≥ 0; `∃ q ∈ Icc (1/2) 2` is 1/2 ≤ q/Q ≤ 2 (and gives q > 0); `forwardScalar (2h) Z q̂ = T`, i.e. T = q̂ - Z² q̂^{2h}, is the paper's τ = q - z²q^{2h} ((3.2) on p. 7) divided by Q, using 2D + 2h = 1 so that z²q^{2h}/Q = Z²q̂^{2h}; `p.1 ^ 2 / (2 * q) ∈ Icc a b` is X_a ≤ R²/(2q̂) = r²/(2q) ≤ X_b, with a, b instantiated downstream as `NominalConeAssembly.activeLeft/activeRight`. `referenceCompact = closure (activeReference …)` supplies "the closed active part". Two differences that do not change the set of slow points used: Lean adds `0 ≤ p.1` (automatic for a radial coordinate), and Lean's set has no `0 < q < q_big` clause — since q/Q ∈ [1/2,2], q < q_big is a constraint on the band index rather than on the slow point (it holds for every point of the band as soon as 2Q ≤ q_big), and Lean carries it instead as the lower band index N in `BaseChartJets.CellIndex`.
